_comment: /deploy-global merges this block into ~/.claude/settings.json idempotently (additive upsert by command — see deploy-global step 13). GATE, not advisory: PreToolUse denies a write to a file a deliverable rule scopes with a short reason naming the rule file ('Held: read <path> first, then re-issue this call.'), and keeps denying until PostToolUse OBSERVES that rule file being read — which is what makes the parallel writes of one turn safe without reading any transcript. The split is the point: PreToolUse never records anything (a read it saw might be refused by the user, since the rule files live outside the project), PostToolUse fires only for calls that ran. PreToolUse carries the executor-dispatch-gate file-edit surface (minus Agent/Task), Grok's tool names (read_file/write/search_replace), the read tools (a read-only agent is gated on its first read of a `readers` rule), and the shell tools for ONE reason: a patch written through the shell (`*** Add File:`) authors files and is gated like apply_patch. PostToolUse carries the read and shell tools for observation only — a `cat`/`sed`/`head` whose ARGUMENT resolves to the rule file releases the gate; `ls`, `rm`, a comment or a redirect do not. HIVE_HARNESS=claude tells the hook which reference root to name and which reason budget to use (Grok reads this same block and is recognized by its own camelCase payload keys, so it keeps the ~264-char clip). No rule text travels in any output. SessionStart on compact|clear drops the session's state so the gate re-arms. Fail-open by construction: state that cannot be written allows, three counted denials (at least 5 s apart) release the rule, any exception exits 0 silently, and HIVE_RULE_DELIVERY=off|0|false|no disables it. Policy: the rule texts under global/rules-situational/ (a rule still under global/rules/ is skipped — Claude Code loads it natively).
